_note: H3b multi-hop questions. Every answer verified by hand against the frozen snapshot on 2026-09-22, BEFORE any run. Grading uses the LAST 'ANSWER:' in the output. Types: number = first number equals expect; first-word = first word equals expect (case-insensitive); name = contains expect (case-insensitive); all = every token appears as a whole word (case-insensitive).

questions.why: runner.mjs: --max-retries default 48 (line 96); retry loop sleeps resetMs ?? retryMinutes*60000 with retryMinutes default 30 (95, 493); retries counts 1..48, break at retries >= maxRetries (490) => 48 x 30 min = 24 h
questions.q: The orchestrator runner (scripts/runner.mjs) is started with --retry-on-limit and otherwise default flags. Every agent run keeps failing with a usage-limit error whose message contains NO parseable reset time. What is the maximum total time, in hours, that the runner will spend sleeping between retries before it gives up?

questions.why: runner.mjs:489 breaks out of the retry loop when !retryOnLimit, before any sleep; --retry-on-limit is an opt-in flag (94)
questions.q: The orchestrator runner (scripts/runner.mjs) is started WITHOUT --retry-on-limit and with otherwise default flags. An agent run hits a usage-limit error. How many times will the runner sleep and retry before it stops?

questions.why: msUntilReset sets the parsed wall-clock time then adds 2 * 60000 ms (runner.mjs:417)

questions.why: msUntilReset returns ms only if <= 12 * 3600000 (runner.mjs:418); otherwise null, and the loop falls back to --retry-minutes
questions.q: In the orchestrator runner, what is the longest wait, in hours, that a parsed limit-reset time can produce before the runner ignores it and falls back to --retry-minutes instead?
